links.lead: LEAD-EXO-minors-guess-and-determine (new; to be filed in knowledge/leads/ecdlp/exotic/)
links.note: Design only. The algorithm is reconstructed from abstracts (the full texts were not opened); open questions are listed in design.md section 'Open risks'.

question: At 20 to 40 bit prime group orders, what is the counted cost, in field-multiplication equivalents, of the reconstructed minors guess-and-determine search for the planted discrete log, against matched negation-map rho on the same planted instances, and does the fitted exponent of that cost in N fall below, or stay above, rho's 0.5?

claims.text: Every completed row of every arm recovers the planted scalar, checked by [k]P = Q outside the runner (exact computation).

The reconstructed minors search costs more FM than matched rho on the same instances at every fitted size, and the fitted exponent alpha_minors of its median cost in N exceeds rho's by a margin whose interval excludes 0.
claims.if_supported: closes LEAD-EXO-minors-guess-and-determine as closed_obstructed (measured, toy scope, reconstructed variant); no statement about the papers' unread full-text variants beyond what the open-question list records
claims.if_not_supported: if alpha_minors upper interval bound is below 0.5 or the log cost ratio slope has an interval below 0, reopen with next_action to full-text re-implementation and larger sizes

claims.text: On the structure-free control matrix the minors search costs the same as on the elliptic-curve matrix within the A/A-calibrated band, i.e. the curve structure gives the search no saving (comparative).
claims.if_supported: the elliptic-curve matrix confers no structural advantage in this variant
claims.if_not_supported: the curve matrix is cheaper than random: a structural effect worth chasing even if rho still wins

claims.text: The minors implementation finds the planted relation in the positive-control family (orders <= 2^20, and an injected zero minor) in every row; a miss invalidates the instrument (exact computation).

hypotheses.statement: H0 (the lead's own analysis): the minors search is a Semaev-style n-sum relation search in determinant form; its charged cost has exponent >= 0.5 in N and is above matched rho at all sizes. H1 (the papers' implied optimism): some size or the fitted exponent shows minors below rho.
hypotheses.mechanism: A zero n x n minor of the evaluation matrix of a Riemann-Roch basis at n points is a relation among points (n points sum to O); finding one among M candidate columns costs about N / C(M, n) minor tests, each charged a determinant, and the product law of LEAD-ICE-generic-oracle-arity-cost-floor says no oracle of this class reaches rho. Prediction: loss, expected null on H1.

predictions.minimum_effect: median FM(minors)/FM(rho) > 1 at each of the sizes 20,24,28,32,36 with the paired bootstrap 95% interval excluding 1
fitted alpha_minors - alpha_rho > 0.05 with 95% interval excluding 0

arms.description: matched negation-map r-adding rho with distinguished points (vOW), same instances, charged in FM
reconstructed minors guess-and-determine search on the elliptic-curve evaluation matrix; every determinant, every elimination step and every function evaluation charged

parameters.n_chosen_by: all three n run on every instance; headline per size is the smallest median FM over n (declared before data); n=2 is the BSGS-equivalent sanity case
parameters.guess_depth: n-1 columns guessed, remaining column determined by cofactor-vector scan

arms.description: rho-neg repeated under a second name with disjoint algorithm seeds
same minors search and same charging on a matrix of the same shape whose columns are uniform in F_p^n (no curve structure); a found zero minor yields no discrete log, cost is time-to-first-zero-minor
same minors code on (a) every prime order curve of 12 to 20 bits and (b) a matrix with an injected dependent column set at a known position; must recover the planted relation

positive.expected_detection: all rows recover k (family a) and the injected zero minor (family b), verified externally; a miss means the implementation, not the method, is broken and no comparative claim stands

null_population.description: matrices with the shape and field of the curve matrix but uniform columns, so any saving relative to them is attributable to curve structure
null_population.generator: columns drawn from SHA-256 counter stream keyed by (size, instance, seed_label) mod p
null_population.why_n: matches instances per size of the decisive arms; 24 gives the bootstrap on a log-cost median a usable interval

factors.name: curve
factors.how: one prime order curve per (size, instance) from generate_prime_order_curve(bits, seed) with seed from the frozen rule; order cross-checked by PARI ellcard; same curve for every arm

factors.name: planted_scalar
factors.how: k uniform in [1,N-1] from SHA-256(protocol_sha256|size|instance), identical across arms

factors.name: inversion_weight
factors.how: FM weights I in {5,10,40} M reported for the sensitivity table; headline I=10 fixed before data

factors.name: n_rows
factors.how: all of n=2,3,4 run; headline min over n of the median, rule frozen

factors.name: budget_cap
factors.how: a row hitting the cap is right-censored, kept as a row

factors.name: threads
factors.how: single threaded; cost is counted not timed

factors.name: host_load
factors.how: recorded; affects wall only, which is not a metric

seed_derivation.note: all seeds are SHA-256 of the protocol hash and the (arm,size,instance,replicate) label; derivation rule frozen with the protocol and recomputed by the checker

instance_sampling.rule: per size in {20,24,28,32,36,40}: 24 instances = (curve, P, Q=kP), curve from generate_prime_order_curve(bits, seed=instance_index) with the first accepted draw; k from SHA-256 stream; the same instance is given to every arm

blinding.how: arms relabelled A..E by a key file hashed in the export; the key is opened after the analysis script outputs are written

power.note: permutation resamples N=9999 give min p 2/(N+1)=2e-4 < alpha/m=0.0125 for the 4 decisive tests (P1, P2, C3 slope difference, C4 detection is exact). Intervals are bootstrap over 24 instances per size; this resolves a cost ratio of ~1.5x per size, not a 10 percent difference. Effect-size power is not claimed.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: estimate from a 1-minute probe: gp ellcard on a 1000003-bit-20 curve returned instantly; Python rho 20-30 bit is seconds per instance; minors time is a model, not measured. Rust implementation required. Capped at 2^40 FM per row; at 4 cores, 8 h worst case.

primary.name: FM
primary.definition: M + S + 10*I + (0 for add/sub/negate/compare), summed over setup that depends on Q, search, linear algebra and the final verification; table-free one-time curve setup and group-order computation uncharged to all arms equally
primary.source: records.jsonl cost.fm and cost.m, cost.s, cost.i

primary.name: fitted exponent
primary.definition: slope of log2 median FM against log2 N over sizes with >= 20 of 24 completed rows, per arm
primary.formula: alpha = OLS slope of log2(median FM over completed rows) on log2(N), over sizes with >= 20 of 24 completed rows

secondary.name: determinant evaluations
secondary.definition: number of n x n determinants or equivalent eliminations charged

secondary.name: group operation equivalents
secondary.definition: rho adds+doubles plus those used to build minors columns; each curve addition or doubling is 1 whatever its field cost, ecbench-compatible

secondary.name: censored rows
secondary.definition: rows stopped at the budget cap / rows attempted

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 6 sizes x 24 instances x (rho, rho A/A, minors n=2,3,4, random-matrix n=2,3,4) rows, plus the positive control at <=20 bits; stop; per row stop at the 2^40 FM cap and record censored
a row whose answer does not verify is recorded as wrong_answer and stops nothing

invalidation_rules: a wrong_answer row, or any positive-control miss, invalidates the minors arm for comparative use
a censored row is kept and is a lower bound; an exponent from a size with fewer than 20 of 24 completed rows is not fitted
wall-clock values are not metrics here

decision_rule.text: Closed-obstructed (confirm): alpha_minors lower 95% bound above 0.5 AND P1 holds at every fitted size AND C-structure shows no saving. Reopen: alpha_minors upper 95% bound below 0.5, or FM ratio minors/rho below 1 with interval excluding 1 at any size >= 32 bits, or the slope of log FM ratio against log N has an interval wholly below 0. Positive control failing: instrument invalid, verdict invalid_measurement. Fewer than 4 fitted sizes: inconclusive.
decision_rule.threshold: as in text; A/A interval of rho must not itself exclude 1 (Bonferroni over m=4 tests); the C-aa interval of rho FM must contain 1, else invalid_measurement
decision_rule.statistic: median FM per size; OLS slope of log2 median FM on log2 N
decision_rule.interval: two-stage bootstrap (instances, then sizes) 95%; permutation p with N=9999
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: alpha difference and per size FM ratio

graphs: log-log FM vs N per arm with fits

inadmissible: changing n_rows rule, guess depth, sizes, seeds or the FM weights after seeing a result
pricing determinants below their elimination operation count, or dropping function-evaluation or column-generation cost
reading a censored row as a completed cost
choosing which Q or curves to report
claiming anything about the papers' full algorithms where the reconstruction differs from them
a stage ratio or wall time as a speedup
extrapolating beyond 2^40 or to a deployed curve
